note:
What I did to data/20-board.json, for the record. Node count 238 -> 108. No id was changed, so nothing outside this file needed rewriting: I checked every other fragment and none of them referenced any id in 20-board.json. All 108 nodes are reachable from mb.pcb / mb.solder / mb.assembly / mb.test / mb.photo.

AUDIT. node scripts/build.mjs exits 0. node scripts/audit.mjs --file 20-board.json examines 108 nodes and reports none of my own mechanical failures, and 24 warnings, all of them one heuristic: a tool, a part or a note sitting in the `assembly` or `logistics` category, where audit.mjs's CAT_OK table admits only `process`. I left those alone on purpose - a wave-soldering machine, a bed of nails and a test cradle are assembly equipment, and `assembly` is the only permitted bucket that fits them. Recategorising them into `metals` or `industry` to silence a warning would be a lie. The four FAILs the audit still prints are tree-wide rule 1a checks for 'Water for a factory', 'Electricity at the factory wall', 'Natural gas: the gas field' and 'Petroleum: light sour crude oil'. I fixed all four edges that were mine - mb.pcb.strip and mb.assembly.cleaning on water, mb.solder.hand and mb.solder.wave.preheat.air on electricity. The remaining 16 + 31 + 12 + 24 offending parents are all in other fragments and belong to their owners.

INGREDIENT LINKS. All 112 input strings across 73 nodes are now exact node ids, so every one resolves on the first try: no name matching, no _ingredients.json table, no prose left dangling. Before this pass: 'electricity' matched nothing at all in 14 places, because the node is a `facility` and build.mjs only indexes part and material names; 'caustic soda' resolved to facility.compressed-air.caustic-soda; 'chlorine' resolved to chem.polycarbonate.phosgene.chlorine; 'screen' resolved to c64.psu.transformer.winding.screen - an interwinding earth screen inside a transformer - on both the solder-mask and the silkscreen steps; 'nickel' resolved to a node inside my own solder-pot subtree; 'propylene' resolved to a propylene node buried in 10-silicon.json's mould-compound branch.

VERIFIED FINDINGS, all preserved. Zero vias and zero plated-through holes; exactly two wire jumpers, E1 and E2; no SMT and no reflow; no conformal coating; HASL as the period pad finish; boards made in Hong Kong; ASSY 250407 / fab 250406 / artwork 251137 / schematic 251138; roughly 1200 unplated holes. The empty 'no plated-barrel line' branch is still there and is now kind note rather than a process, so it reads as a recorded absence instead of an unfinished step.
